We support this position by comparing membership-inference evaluations across four prominent autoregressive EHR generators, highlighting inconsistent evaluation practices in patient representations and attack procedures. We evaluate trajectory reconstruction from partial context and introduce randomly assigned patient-level canaries to distinguish memorised associations from clinical generalisation. We examine these methods in a GPT-2-style model deliberately overfit to 1,000 MIMIC-IV patient trajectories, creating a controlled setting in which memorisation should be readily detectable. The model systematically recovers training patients' canaries, and their trajectory reconstruction approaches perfect accuracy with increasing context. Held-out patients show no systematic canary recovery, while reconstruction remains low and improves only marginally with additional context. These experiments establish a positive-control baseline for further evaluation of these methods in realistically trained models.
articles.title_zh: 合成EHR生成器应像LLMS一样接受审计

articles.title: RadAG: Reward-Adversarial Attention Guidance for Efficient Inference-Time Alignment of Diffusion Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion and flow-based models have achieved remarkable success in generation, yet their samples often remain suboptimal in fidelity and text alignment. Two lines of inference-time methods address this: extrapolation guidance, such as classifier-free guidance (CFG) and its variants, and reward guidance, which aligns samples with reward models of human preference. Extrapolation guidance needs only forward passes, but it builds its reference by heuristic rules unrelated to the reward and therefore cannot steer sampling toward a given reward. Gradient-based reward guidance steers sampling directly toward a higher reward, but backpropagates through the entire generator at every step. This trade-off raises the question of whether extrapolation guidance can steer sampling toward a higher reward without a full backward pass. To answer this, we introduce Reward-Adversarial Attention Guidance (RadAG), which constructs the reference by perturbing the attention logits of a single block against their reward gradient and extrapolates away from it. We prove that this update increases the reward of the clean estimate to first order, while its backward pass stops at the perturbed block instead of traversing the entire generator. On FLUX.2-klein-4B and 9B with PickScore and aesthetic rewards, RadAG achieves the highest target reward in every setting with 30-65% less time than gradient-based and candidate-based baselines.
articles.title_zh: RadAG:高效推导-时间对接扩散模型的奖励-异常注意指导

articles.title: Pixel Auto-Encoder: Reconstructing Language Model Activations Through Pixel Art
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interpreting the high-dimensional internal representations of large language models (LLMs) remains a challenging problem. Recent approaches have explored translating these representations into human-understandable forms, particularly natural language. In this work, we explore the use of images as an alternative target modality for interpreting LLM activations. As a first step toward this goal, we introduce Pixel Auto-Encoder, which converts intermediate LLM activations into $32 \times 32$, 32-color pixel art and reconstructs them for subsequent computation within the model. By encouraging the intermediate representations to resemble predefined concept images, we investigate whether LLM activations can be expressed visually while preserving the model's language capabilities. We find that the model can produce target-aligned images for some concepts, and that replacing pixel representations with concept images can influence next-token predictions. However, we also observe a trade-off between visual alignment and language-model performance, as well as sensitivity to pixel-level changes that are difficult to interpret visually. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and limitations of image-based representations of LLM activations.
articles.title_zh: 像素自动编码器:通过像素艺术重建语言示范活性

articles.title: Hidden Sensitivity in LLM Pre-training: A Dynamic System View
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Large Language Model (LLM) pre-training, loss curves can conceal substantial instability, i.e., even small perturbations may lead to dramatically different predictions while leaving loss nearly unchanged. To investigate this phenomenon and reveal the underlying mechanisms, we first formulate LLM pre-training as a non-autonomous dynamical system that jointly evolves model weights and Adam optimizer states. Based on this formulation, we introduce a normalized sensitivity score in optimizer-relative coordinates to identify sensitive training checkpoints. At one such checkpoint, a weight perturbation of only 10^(-5) leads to 35.7% disagreement in top-1 predictions and 16.2% disagreement in benchmark answers after 200 training steps, with only 0.8% of greedy generations remaining identical despite similar validation losses. Furthermore, we find that perturbations to Adam's first and second moments induce comparably large effects, with similar sensitivity patterns observed in OLMo-1B. Finally, guided by our diagnostic, targeted stabilization reduces top-1 disagreement to 0.83% and increases generation exact match to 88.3%, at the cost of a 0.11-nat increase in validation loss. Our findings reveal a hidden form of optimizer-state-dependent sensitivity in LLM pre-training that conventional loss-based evaluations may overlook, while demonstrating its potential for diagnosis and mitigation.
articles.title_zh: LLM 预训中的隐藏灵敏度:动态系统视图

articles.title: AgriManager: A Framework and Benchmark for LLM-RL Generalization in Agricultural Management
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agricultural management is heterogeneous along two axes. The first is distributional shift within a fixed task interface: weather, crops, and prices vary across years and locations while sensors, actions, and objective stay fixed. The second is structural shift across interfaces: different farms expose different observed variables, available actions, and management objectives. We formalize the second axis as schema shift: variation in the policy-facing schema $\Sigma = (\Sigma_O, \Sigma_A, \Sigma_R)$ between training and deployment. We test whether LLM-RL generalizes across both axes with AgriManager, to our knowledge the first framework that trains LLM policies with RL across multiple process-based crop simulators, unifying DSSAT, WOFOST, and Cycles. We design a three-tier generalization ladder: Tier 1 within-schema distributional shift, Tier 2 single-axis schema shift along $\Sigma_O / \Sigma_A / \Sigma_R$, Tier 3 compositional schema shift across simulators, all scored on a frozen held-out test suite with three training seeds per method. Within fixed schemas, Qwen3-4B trained by RL with explicit reasoning exceeds neural-network PPO trained with the same interaction budget; without reasoning, training stalls near no-action where the reward penalizes input use. Under single-axis schema shift, $\Sigma_O$ transfer needs decision-critical state, $\Sigma_A$ results are consistent with joint action-menu coverage, and with reasoning a policy trained on yield alone transfers to unseen objectives. Under compositional schema shift, single-source training mostly hurts zero-shot transfer across simulators, and a unified policy trained only on other combinations of the same components recovers about 86% of the gain of a specialist trained on the target combination on DSSAT and stays below the specialists on the WOFOST and Cycles profit targets. Project page: https://agrimanager-framework.github.io
articles.title_zh: AgriManager:农业管理中的LLM-RL通用框架和基准

articles.title: Dynamic Model Merging with Multi-Layer Aggregated Routing Evidence
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic model merging aims to retain the efficiency of a unified model while better preserving task-specific expertise through input-dependent routing at both the task and head levels. However, even the routing components of the state-of-the-art approach remain limited: the task routing is highly sensitive to the choice of routing layer, whereas the head routing relies on simple max-logit competition. To address these limitations, we propose multi-layer aggregated routing evidence (MATE) as a unified mechanism for improving both task and head routing. Specifically, we first introduce a metric to quantify task routing separability across different layers. Empirical analysis of this metric reveals that different layers provide complementary evidence for identifying the tasks relevant to an input. Motivated by this observation, MATE selects multiple informative layers according to their routing separability and aggregates their layer-wise routing scores to produce a more robust signal that can be directly used for task selection. Moreover, we observe that this signal also encodes useful information about the suitability of the corresponding classification heads. This motivates us to further combine the MATE signal with the max-logit score to guide classification head selection. Extensive experiments on vision benchmarks demonstrate that MATE consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance.
articles.title_zh: 动态模型与多层排列式聚合证据合并

articles.title: Interaction Retention and Output-Likelihood Training in Parallel Sampling
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parallel samplers such as masked diffusion language models generate several coordinates per step from conditional marginals and randomize which coordinates are generated together, so even exact conditionals return a distorted distribution. We give an exact local account of this distortion. Around any full-support product law, the Gram operator of the sampler's response is diagonal in the interaction decomposition, and its eigenvalues are retention probabilities: the probability that an interaction has a unique latest-revealed coordinate. This retention spectrum determines the exact frontier between output accuracy and conditional calibration, its regularization path, and the population response of finite-mixture likelihood training. For pairwise interactions it yields a sharp dichotomy. Under homogeneous retention, output-likelihood training is equivalent to a single context gain; heterogeneous retention opens correction directions beyond any scalar, with an advantage bounded by an explicit heterogeneity gap. On binarized digits and MNIST, output-likelihood training within a heterogeneous schedule library lowers calibrated test negative log-likelihood in all twelve paired comparisons, and the gain survives pair-specific recalibration and a stronger path optimizer. For a frozen 169.6-million-parameter masked diffusion language model, serially normalized context gains are 1.070 and 1.056 at 8 and 16 rounds, against the predicted values 1.134 and 1.058.
articles.title_zh: 互动保留和平行抽样输出关联培训

articles.title: MolReJev: Decision Models Are In-Context Molecular Predictors
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecular prediction helps prioritize compounds for screening. Specialized predictors are trained for a fixed set of tasks, limiting cross-task generalization. Language models can condition on task descriptions and have recently shown promise in molecular prediction. However, generating answers token by token adds inference cost, and general-purpose models often lack task-specific molecular knowledge. We thus propose MolReJev, which combines Jev-style candidate scoring with in-context learning (ICL) on a language model. MolReJev retrieves similar labeled examples from existing task data and scores candidate labels jointly in one forward pass. ICL improves predictions from the released general-purpose Kev checkpoint and the separately trained MolReJev. For the trained model, gains span all evaluation groups, including held-out tasks, and extend to compounds absent from training. MolReJev generally outperforms MolecularGPT on matched evaluations and nearest-neighbor prediction with the same examples. With four examples, MolReJev and a trained text baseline achieve similar ROC-AUC, with higher measured throughput for MolReJev. These results show that decision models can serve as in-context molecular predictors for compounds, drug pairs, and reactions.
articles.title_zh: MollReJev:决定模型是内在分子预测器

articles.title: S$^2$LMR: Supervised Sequential Long-Context Multi-Step Retriever
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-step retrieval over long contexts is a key capability for retrieval-augmented generation, but strong existing approaches are costly and complex to train. Supervised retrievers are far simpler and cheaper, yet they fall well behind in this setting. We show that this gap stems not from supervised training itself, but from three misalignments between training and inference: easy training negatives, noisy retrieval prefixes, and position-agnostic scoring. Guided by this analysis, we introduce S$^2$LMR, a simple yet effective supervised sequential retriever that models multi-step retrieval as the evolution of an explicit textual state encoded by a single shared Transformer. On long-context reasoning, multi-hop QA, and needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks with context lengths ranging from 4K to 10M tokens, S$^2$LMR achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods, substantially outperforming prior supervised retrievers. Notably, it requires only $\sim$2 hours of training on a single A6000 for contexts of up to 10M tokens, while remaining robust across a wide range of hyperparameter settings.
articles.title_zh: S$^2$LMR: 被监督的序列长文本多步骤检索器

articles.title: Do Larger Fully Connected Neural Networks Generalize Better?
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Greater neural-network capacity does not necessarily yield better performance on unseen data. This study investigates whether a deeper, fully connected neural-network architecture generalizes better than a shallower architecture on the Fashion-MNIST dataset. We compare two architectures under two learning rates and two L2-regularization settings, producing eight configurations. The architectures contain 95,410 and 561,470 trainable parameters, respectively, an approximately 5.9-fold difference. Checkpoints and the final configuration are selected by validation loss, and all configurations are evaluated on a held-out test set. The selected larger configuration achieves 89.82% validation accuracy and 88.77% test accuracy. Selecting the lowest-validation-loss configuration within each architecture yields test accuracies of 88.77% and 88.52%, respectively, a difference of 0.25 percentage points. Across matched training settings, the larger architecture achieves higher test accuracy in only one of four comparisons. Class-level errors are concentrated among visually similar garment categories, and qualitative pixel-removal analyses suggest sensitivity to shape and boundaries. Overall, the findings suggest that increasing architectural capacity alone does not guarantee better generalization, highlighting the importance of considering optimization and regularization when selecting neural-network architectures.
articles.title_zh: 更大型的全能连接神经网络实现全面化了吗?.

articles.title: A Finite-Rate Selection Law for Annealed Gibbs Sampling
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Annealed Gibbs sampling samples a multimodal model by redrawing one variable at a time from its conditional distribution as the temperature falls from a high value, where the distribution is broad, to the target temperature. Each run ends in a single mode, and unbiased Monte Carlo estimates require the runs to end in each mode in proportion to its probability under the model. At a finite cooling rate this can fail. We measure the error by $c$, the fraction of the model's log-odds between two modes that the samples retain. In the Curie--Weiss model, where a weak external field favors one of two modes, each run selects its mode near the transition at which the modes form, and rarely switches once they have separated. Near the transition, the random fluctuations of the Gibbs updates still outweigh the weak field, which therefore biases the choice of mode only slightly. Building on the selection probability of Kondepudi and coworkers, we derive a law for $c$ that agrees with an exact computation to within $2\%$ on nine linear cooling ramps. For the Hopfield model, whose modes are stored patterns and their negatives, we derive a factor by which competition among patterns raises $c$. The $c$ measured over random pattern sets lies within $3$--$6\%$ of its prediction, but single pattern sets depart from it, contrary to its derivation.
articles.title_zh: Annaled Gibbs抽样的有限比例选择法

articles.title: DiRGeo: Learning Directional Geometry of Visual Representations
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional geometric measures of visual representations are symmetric, assigning equal costs to forward and reverse motion along the same path. We propose DiRGeo, a framework for learning directional geometry over frozen visual representations. Grounded in Randers geometry, DiRGeo learns a state-dependent directional field from ordered image trajectories through self-supervised contrast, without semantic labels. Sphere-tangent correction and attractor-relative decomposition distinguish learned directional structure from normalization artifacts and common convergence. Experiments across 17 visual processes, three encoder families, and multiple representation depths demonstrate consistent directional discrimination and whole-path asymmetry beyond simple attractor-based explanations. The learned fields become increasingly process-specific in deeper representations, while natural-video experiments reveal event-dependent directional preferences. As functional validation, DiRGeo guides restoration selection. These results establish directional geometry as a useful complement to symmetric representation analysis.
articles.title_zh: DIRGeo:视觉表现的学习方向几何

articles.title: Pain Reassessment from Pulse Waveforms with Language Model Explanations
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Routine photoplethysmography (PPG) offers a continuous physiological signal for pain reassessment between self-reports. Whether prior recordings provide an individualized physiological reference beyond care-process timing remains unresolved. Across 52,082 report-linked assessments from 21,514 patients in MIMIC-III critical care and MC-MED emergency care, we evaluate a workflow that pairs longitudinal PPG representations with local evidence-linked language interpretation. Among 27 methods, source-selected full-history models achieved average precision of 0.824 from critical to emergency care and 0.822 in reverse. Removing historical pulse-run representations while retaining reassessment availability and elapsed time lowered critical-to-emergency four-hour within-patient concordance from 0.718 to 0.534. This comparison supports the contribution of prior pulse-run representations to within-patient ordering beyond timing cues. Across 2,905 test patients, a local Qwen model interpreting frozen predictions achieved a 94.7% patient-equal pass rate on automated evidence checks after at most one revision. Longitudinal pulse context and evidence-linked language interpretation support a patient-centred workflow for pain reassessment.
articles.title_zh: 用语言模型解释从脉冲波形进行疼痛再评估

articles.title: ARC: Adaptive Rollout Control for Efficient Synchronous LLM Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synchronous reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models proceeds through a repeated rollout--barrier--update loop. Each update must wait for a fixed number of complete, group-relative training samples, yet individual response lengths and reward outcomes vary widely and only emerge as generation progresses. Static admission and unconditional completion therefore leave accelerators idle in some steps, and waste computation generating samples that will never contribute to the current update. We present ARC, a closed-loop rollout architecture that governs synchronous RL rollout at group granularity. ARC uses \textit{Calibrated Streaming Backfill} to judge from partial observations whether a group is still worth completing, backfilling a fresh candidate immediately when it is not; \textit{Deferred Group Completion} to park an uncertain early stop and resume it later instead of discarding it outright, bounded by a resume-cycle limit that guarantees termination; and \textit{Adaptive Admission} and \textit{Pipelining} to order admitted samples by early-measured duration and to admit further candidates only while expected supply still falls short of the target number of accepted groups. Under online evaluation, ARC reduces rollout time by $37.4\%$, a $1.60\times$ speedup, and improves effective GRPO throughput by $50.1\%$ over existing baselines, while directly recovering 98.9\% of the training groups that would ultimately have been kept.
articles.title_zh: ARC: 高效同步LLM强化学习的可适应推出控制

articles.title: On Adaptive Step Sizes for Eligibility Traces in Deep Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms store agent-environment interactions in a replay buffer and later learn by sampling transitions from it. However, this approach can be memory-inefficient and can delay learning because the agent can learn from a transition only when the buffer samples it. Additionally, most of these methods use one-step or short multi-step temporal-difference (TD) updates, which are slow at credit assignment. An alternative approach is to learn from the stream of observations as they arrive without relying on a buffer. Eligibility-trace algorithms allow these incremental updates and can also assign credit over many steps. These algorithms were common with linear function approximation but have only recently been used in deep RL. Basic questions, such as how to use vector step sizes with eligibility traces in the deep RL setting, remain open. In this work, we first show that adaptive vector step sizes must be part of the eligibility trace to keep the equivalence between the forward and backward views. We then show that the step sizes of common optimizers, such as Adam, do not have an online backward view. We introduce a new optimizer, Function-Space Distance (FSD), that maintains the forward-backward equivalence. We test four eligibility-trace algorithms covering semi-gradient and gradient TD updates, as well as value-based and actor-critic methods. We show that FSD performs better than SGD or naively applied Adam. The resulting algorithms outperform or match other streaming methods and are comparable to or better than PPO, which uses a buffer, in most environments. Code available at https://github.com/esraaelelimy/ada_traces
articles.title_zh: 关于深度强化学习中资格追踪的适应性步骤大小

articles.title: Ziv Meets Sumcheck: Zero-Knowledge Proofs of Floating-Point LLM Inference
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29188v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-knowledge proofs can show that a neural network produced a given output without revealing the network, but current systems for language models prove integer approximations of the model rather than the floating-point arithmetic that is actually deployed. Proving floating-point matrix multiplication has been regarded as hard, because rounding after every addition makes the result depend on the order of the additions. We avoid this obstacle by proving the correctly rounded product, in which every dot product is computed exactly and rounded once. This result is independent of the hardware and at least as accurate as standard kernels. We give an interactive proof for this relation whose cost is close to that of integer matrix multiplication, with roughly a thousand times fewer committed values than per-operation floating-point circuits need constraints, extend it to every layer of a transformer, and give a privacy construction for the complete argument whose zero knowledge we prove under explicit hypotheses. We implement the system and prove the full forward pass of GPT-2 small, including all twelve blocks and the output over the whole vocabulary, in 19 minutes on two processor cores; verification takes 21 seconds. The verifier rejects all 236 attacks we tested, and the model's outputs agree with high-precision inference at least as closely as standard 16-bit inference does.
articles.title_zh: Ziv 满足总和:浮点LLM的零知识证明 推论

articles.title: THETA: Heat Diffusion as a Structural Prior for Cross-Domain Transfer in Graph Foundation Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph foundation models (GFMs) aim to learn transferable representations across domains with heterogeneous node attributes and graph structures. However, relations inferred from node attributes can rely on domain-specific feature semantics, limiting their transferability to unseen graphs, particularly in low-label regimes. We propose THETA (Topology-aware HEat-based TrAnsfer), a graph foundation model that leverages Heat Kernel Signatures (HKS) as a topology-based structural prior for cross-domain transfer. By characterizing nodes' heat-return behavior across diffusion scales, HKS provides a common structural descriptor across graphs without requiring aligned attribute semantics, complementing feature-based relations with information about local and multiscale connectivity. THETA incorporates this prior into both pre-training and few-shot adaptation. During pre-training, it combines HKS with node attributes to construct refined graph views and trains a shared encoder via contrastive learning. During adaptation, it uses HKS to guide edge-weight adjustment and prototype refinement while keeping the encoder frozen and retaining the contribution of labeled support nodes. Through HKS, THETA uses structural information from heat diffusion to guide both representation learning and few-shot adaptation with unlabeled target-domain data. Extensive experiments across diverse graph domains demonstrate that THETA consistently outperforms existing baselines on downstream tasks, highlighting the value of heat diffusion as a structural prior for transferable graph representations.
articles.title_zh: THETA:热分泌作为图基模型中跨域转移的结构前置

articles.title: NANO: Unifying Missingness and Input Uncertainty in Tabular Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Missing values are common in tabular data, yet current approaches to handling them often overlook two dimensions. First, an observed value may be uncertain, while a Not-Observed (N.O.) value may still have a reasonable estimate. Inputs should therefore span a continuous spectrum from no evidence to a fully trusted observation. Second, Not-Applicable (N.A.) means that no meaningful value exists for a record, yet this semantic state often lacks explicit representation. To address both dimensions, we introduce NANO, a unified plug-in for input encoding that fits most token-based architectures. Guided by Bayesian evidence weighting, NANO adjusts the influence of a supplied value according to confidence, with all zero-confidence estimates mapped to the same N.O. representation. NANO accepts, but does not require, per-example confidence information during training or inference. For N.A., a separate representation enables models to encode inapplicability and its schema-defined reasons into context. Experiments across eleven datasets and nine backbones show that mixed-confidence training enables a single NANO model to generalize across inference confidence levels, remaining competitive without estimates and improving steadily as estimate reliability and confidence increase. The effectiveness of NANO's handling of N.A. is further demonstrated on three augmented datasets.
articles.title_zh: NANO: 统一表格学习中的缺失和输入不确定性

articles.title: Tissot indicatrix for location encoders: Characterizing local distortion in learned geographic embeddings
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the increasing adoption of geographic artificial intelligence, location encoders are widely used to map geographic coordinates to learned embeddings for tasks in Earth observation and geospatial modeling. Similar to map projections, location encoders can distort geographic space, that is, equal-distance displacements in different directions can result in unequal embedding changes. However, such distortion remains largely unexamined, and it can propagate into downstream applications. We adapt Tissot's indicatrix, a cartographic tool for map projection distortion, to characterize this distortion. At each location, we compare encoder outputs at equal distances in 32 directions and fit a tensor, represented by an ellipse, whose elongation (anisotropy) and orientation describe the local distortion. The fit requires only encoder outputs without access to model internals and is validated against references with known geometry. By applying the method to thirteen released checkpoints of five encoder families, we find that distortions vary across space and inherit the input geometry to varying degrees, closely in GeoCLIP with its Equal Earth input (anisotropy correlation of 0.88) and weakly or moderately in the other encoders. The distortion also affects the locations an encoder treats as neighbors. Within 1km of 20 query sites, the 40 nearest neighbors in geographic and embedding space overlap by a median of only 57.5--87.5% across the checkpoints, while the fitted ellipses select exactly the same embedding neighbors in 265 of 299 comparisons. These findings provide a geographic basis for assessing location encoders, and the accompanying eTissot package implements the methods for user-specified encoders.
articles.title_zh: Tissot indicatrix 用于定位编码器:在已学习的地理嵌入中描述本地扭曲

articles.title: OAT3D: A Generative Model for 3D Shape- and Resolution-Free Structural Topology Optimization
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topology optimization determines how material should be distributed within a design domain to optimize structural performance under prescribed loads, supports, and constraints. The problems are highly nonconvex, and conventional solvers require repeated finite element analyses, making high-resolution 3D topology optimization computationally expensive. Data-driven approaches face an additional bottleneck: generating training datasets requires solving large numbers of these costly problems, so existing work in data-driven topology optimization primarily focuses on 2D problems. Large-scale 3D datasets remain scarce, and existing models remain limited in problem scale and boundary-condition diversity. Here, we introduce Optimize Any Topology-3D (OAT3D), a generative model for high-resolution 3D structural topology optimization. OAT3D introduces a novel sparse problem encoding to represent load and fixity conditions and combines a sparse volumetric variational autoencoder with a conditional diffusion transformer. We construct a dataset of 501,865 optimized topologies, generated using 51,800 GPU-hours and encompassing structures with up to one million elements and substantially more complex loading and support configurations than any existing structural topology optimization dataset. To our knowledge, this is the largest dataset for 3D topology optimization structures. Trained on this dataset, OAT3D generates structures at 512$^3$ resolution and achieves a $44.9\times$ speedup for raw candidate structure generation or $3.65\times$ speedup to reach similar compliance over conventional topology optimization. These contributions expand the scale and diversity of data-driven topology optimization for three-dimensional structural design.
articles.title_zh: OAT3D: 三维形状和分辨率结构地形优化的基因模型

articles.title: Look Back: Reinforcement Learning with Counterfactual World Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents in complex, stochastic environments must contend with dynamics that can exceed their world models' predictive capacity and randomness that obscure the consequences of their actions. We hypothesize that, compared to imagining entirely new trajectories in such complex environments, it can be easier to transform observed trajectories with alternative actions. Counterfactual world models condition on observations to predict alternative outcomes under the same underlying environmental randomness, using experience as a reference for predicting action-dependent changes. We present a policy gradient estimator, REINFORCE Look Back (RLB), that uses counterfactual returns as baselines to distinguish action effects from environmental luck, and prove conditions for unbiasedness and variance reduction. In settings where environmental evolution is harder to predict than action-induced changes, we show that counterfactual world models are easier to learn and support better policy learning than ordinary world models. Our findings suggest that counterfactual thinking can help agents learn effective behavior without independently reproducing the full complexity of their worlds.
articles.title_zh: 回想:用反事实世界模式加强学习

articles.title: Dually Constrained Parameter Projection for Continual Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continual learning requires a model to learn multiple new tasks sequentially while retaining performance on previous tasks. Projecting model parameters onto the Jacobian null space of previous tasks after unconstrained training on a new task has emerged as an effective paradigm. However, unidirectional projection merely minimizes the parameter distance to the new-task optimum, overlooking the new-task loss landscape. To address this limitation, we propose DUET, a bidirectional projection algorithm that imposes Jacobian null-space constraints from both previous and new tasks during post-training projection. Specifically, DUET formulates the post-training adjustment as a dually constrained optimization problem. It minimizes the distance between parameters before and after training on a new task, subject to loss preserving constraints on both tasks. To solve the optimization problem, we develop an alternating bidirectional projection algorithm, whose convergence is guaranteed by the contraction mapping theorem. For reliable multi-step projection, we rectify existing step size selection criteria via an effective-rank aware formulation, overcoming their failure under rank-deficient Jacobians. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DUET consistently outperforms existing unidirectional projection methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple datasets.
articles.title_zh: 继续学习的双重限制参数预测

articles.title: QASparse: Query-Adaptive Sparse Attention with Tailored Budgets and Tokens
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-sequence inference in large language models is constrained by the high cost of prefilling, where dense attention scales quadratically with context length. Exploiting similarity across attention heads offers a way to reduce redundant computation. Prior approaches in this direction have relied on localized query observations to determine head-level computation reuse or budget allocation. However, inter-head similarity does not imply uniform query requirements, leaving adaptation to varying budget needs and selection preferences across query regions a key challenge. We introduce QASparse, a Query-Adaptive Sparse attention mechanism with hardware-efficient execution. QASparse preserves the efficiency of shared cross-head importance estimation while adapting computational budgets and token selections to query requirements, and it executes these dynamic sparse decisions through dedicated kernels. Its query adaptivity stems from two complementary innovations: Local Budget Regression models local variations in computational demand along query positions to estimate budgets for different query regions and attention heads; Boundary Voting lets queries within each head vote over candidates near the selection cutoff using actual query/key scores, refining the retained set while preserving the initial selection size. To reduce the execution overhead of dynamic budgets, we further design length-specialized selection kernels that efficiently support query-adaptive sparse patterns across context lengths. Together, these designs efficiently combine shared estimation with local decisions while adapting both how much attention is computed and which interactions are retained. Experimental results demonstrate improved benchmark scores and faster prefill attention computation compared with existing sparse attention baselines.
articles.title_zh: QASparse:与量身定做的预算和托肯斯的 查询- 辅助分解关注

articles.title: Hybrid state-space and attention neural operators for nonlinear structural dynamics under environmental loading
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The computational burden of repeated nonlinear time-history analyses limits their application for structural assessment and design. We therefore propose DeepOJamba, a hybrid neural operator that combines selective state-space recurrence with full attention to predict the structural response history due to dynamic loading. Physical-parameter conditioning and predicted-state transfer between sequences enable a single trained operator to represent varying system conditions and generate response histories beyond its training sequence length. DeepOJamba is evaluated on a 15~MW monopile offshore wind turbine under wind and wave loading. The proposed operator is compared to pure attention, pure state-space, Fourier, and DeepONet operators and is found to give the lowest window error on every channel and the lowest closed-loop fatigue and ultimate-load errors of $9.4\%$ and $6.0\%$, against $14.6\%$ and $8.7\%$ for the next-best pure attention operator examined. Moreover, on sea states outside the training wave band, the error slightly increases by approximately $0.4$ percentage points. Pure state-space operators can approach similar low errors only with a much wider convolution kernel tuned to the tower eigenperiod, which increases the training cost by $40\%$. In all, the results obtained support hybrid neural operators for robust long-duration structural response and demand prediction.
articles.title_zh: 环境负荷下非线性结构动态的混合状态-空间和注意力神经操作员

articles.title: DeciForm: Incorporating Task Structure into Decision Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decision models unify candidate selection, Boolean judgment, and numerical scoring within a single model. Their answer spaces nevertheless carry different structures: classification candidates form an unordered set, while numerical scores have an intrinsic order and distance. We introduce Deciform, which incorporates these distinctions into computation and supervision. Candidate-free queries and isolated candidate branches support consistent classification under reordering. A log--spherical objective trains candidate probabilities, while a decimal-prefix readout combines individual-value and interval-weighted cumulative supervision for numerical scoring. Shared adapters, task-private residuals, and output-channel gains support joint adaptation. On a shared 15,000-request test set, Deciform improves all three decision metrics on Qwen and ModernBERT; source-normalized errors support the Score gains across the data mixture. Canonicalized joint encoding also eliminates tested order flips, while isolation further improves prediction metrics. Separate objective studies and main-configuration ablations examine the classification and numerical components. After one epoch of MIND-small adaptation, Deciform improves multi-positive news ranking on both backbones. These results support matching encoding and supervision to answer-space structure within a unified decision interface.
articles.title_zh: DDeciForm:将任务结构纳入决策模式

articles.title: SleepXA: Composing Pretrained Neural and Cardiac Foundation Models for Sleep Representation Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physiological signals recorded during sleep provide synchronized views of neural, cardiac, respiratory, and other bodily systems, while preserving modality-specific information. Existing EEG and ECG foundation models already capture rich but distinct physiological structure, motivating an alternative to training a multimodal sleep model from scratch: composing existing pretrained models. We introduce SleepXA, a framework that uses synchronized polysomnography (PSG) to compose independently pretrained neural and cardiac foundation models. SleepXA combines pretrained EEG and ECG encoders with lightweight encoders for additional PSG modalities, and learns shared and modality-specific representations through sleep-guided alignment. We pretrain SleepXA on 9,230 overnight PSG recordings from three large cohorts and evaluate it on 27 downstream tasks spanning sleep representation, clinical and disease prediction, and daytime physiological transfer. SleepXA ranks among the top two methods on 22 of 27 tasks. Controlled experiments further show consistent benefits across sensor configurations and EEG-ECG backbone choices, while pretrained initialization outperforms architecture-matched training from scratch and SleepXA surpasses alternative multimodal composition strategies. These results suggest that synchronized multimodal physiology can serve as a natural interface for composing existing physiological foundation models, yielding reusable representations that extend beyond sleep to clinical and daytime physiological settings.
articles.title_zh: SleepXA:为睡眠代表学习建立训练有素的神经和心脏病基金会模型

articles.title: BenchMint: From Real-World Tasks to Executable Benchmarks
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) need evaluations of everyday reasoning and tool use, such as planning itineraries under user constraints and grounding numerical answers in evidence. We introduce BenchMint, an automated benchmark-construction workflow, and Daily-Life, its collection of 100 selected tasks across 11 real-world domains. BenchMint jointly constructs tasks and scoring criteria from the same source documents. Language-model judges assess possible answers against these criteria using tool traces and private evidence. We report 26 model/harness configurations, including GPT, Claude and Gemini families; 17 have complete domain profiles. These are descriptive configuration results, not a controlled model ranking. In one selected travel task, we corrected the reference total from 320 to 380 minutes while keeping both answers unchanged. The incorrect answer's arithmetic verdict switched from pass to fail; the correct answer's switched from fail to pass. With one ballot per cell, this exposes a reference error without establishing repeatability or collection-wide validity. Incomplete construction comparisons establish no general advantage of joint authoring or feedback-guided revision.
articles.title_zh: BeachMint: 从现实世界任务到可执行基准

articles.title: HKD-ACPA: Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation Adversarial Cyber-Physical Attacks in Power Grids
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning-based algorithms assist power-grid control centers in localizing transmission-line attacks, yet existing adversarial attacks typically require white-box access or repeated online queries. We study a practical zero-query setting in which an adversary coordinates physical, denial-of-service (DoS), and false data injection (FDI) attacks using only local measurements and historical detector outputs. To bridge the input-view asymmetry between local adversarial observations and DoS-masked control-center measurements, we propose Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation Adversarial Cyber-Physical Attacks (HKD-ACPA). HKD-ACPA distills historical detector predictions into a heterogeneous graph surrogate ensemble and trains a residual calibration module to correct the view-induced logit discrepancy. Over this calibrated surrogate, we formulate sparse, magnitude-bounded FDI synthesis with a group-balanced objective that jointly induces missed detections and false alarms, and solve the resulting hybrid discrete--continuous problem via bi-level projected gradient-based proximal policy optimization (PGPPO). Experiments on the IEEE 30-bus and 118-bus systems show that HKD-ACPA outperforms all surrogate-based baselines across every sparsity budget and surpasses online-query attacks in eight of ten system--budget settings without querying the detector model.
articles.title_zh: HKD-ACPA:异质知识分解 网络-物理攻击强网

articles.title: RumiFold: Teaching an LLM to Natively Fold Proteins and Reason About Their Function
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can we teach a general-purpose language model to fold proteins? And if so, what does learning to fold enable beyond structure prediction itself? We introduce RumiFold, a pretrained chat model that learns to predict protein structures directly from its own hidden states. RumiFold processes proteins through repeated folding passes, then uses these folded representations to answer questions in natural language. It achieves folding accuracy comparable to dedicated single-representation models such as SimpleFold, alongside state-of-the-art performance on Gene Ontology protein function prediction and free-text function description. We find that folding pretraining organizes the model's hidden states around protein function, creating an internal per-residue workspace that is biologically grounded. Causal interventions show that this folded workspace links structure and language when RumiFold predicts function, providing rich representations for biomolecular reasoning. We see RumiFold as a step toward native biomolecular intelligence: where protein-based computations and language-based reasoning become integrated capabilities of general-purpose language models. Code, data, and models are available at: https://rumifold.baulab.info
articles.title_zh: RumiFold: 教授一个 LLM 给原生的粗体蛋白及其功能的理由

articles.title: OnCache: Learning Dynamic Caching Schedules for Efficient Diffusion Inference
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion models have revolutionized generative tasks but incur high inference latency due to iterative denoising. Cache-based strategies accelerate inference by reusing intermediate features, yet they largely rely on static, sample-agnostic schedules. Our empirical analysis reveals two factors that these schedules overlook. (i) denoising dynamics and computational requirements vary across prompts, motivating adaptive computation allocation. (ii) sensitivity to caching errors varies across timesteps, so static schedules may reuse features at error-sensitive steps or waste computation at less sensitive ones. We therefore propose OnCache, a dynamic caching framework that makes prompt-adaptive decisions online about how much computation to allocate and when to refresh cached features. A policy is trained offline on paired compute and cache continuations from identical denoising states, using differences in terminal fidelity and the number of function evaluations (NFE) to account for the downstream consequences of each decision. To further improve the generation quality, a neural corrector compensates for caching-induced errors and mitigates their accumulation throughout the denoising trajectory. Both components are lightweight and introduce negligible additional inference latency. On FLUX.1-dev, OnCache achieves a nearly $3\times$ generation speedup at $1024^2$ resolution, with LPIPS of $0.156$ and SSIM of $0.860$. We further extend OnCache to video generation on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, achieving state-of-the-art efficiency--quality trade-offs across both modalities.
articles.title_zh: OnCache: 高效传播的学习动态缓存表

articles.title: Learning Global Probabilistic Explanations
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interpreting the predictions of complex black-box classifiers remains a central challenge in explainable artificial intelligence. While local explanations clarify individual predictions, there is a significant need for global probabilistic explanations that capture a model's overall behavior across the input distribution. Such an explanation is a small subset $K$ of features, whose relevance is measured by the expected probability, over a random input $\mathbf x$, that the classifier assigns the same label to $\mathbf x$ and to a random input agreeing with $\mathbf x$ on $K$. In this study, we investigate the task of identifying maximally relevant global explanations under a cardinality constraint, focusing on product distributions with full support on discrete feature spaces. We introduce a spectral explainer that leverages membership queries to the black-box classifier and employs Fourier-analytic, junta-learning methods to produce probably approximately correct (PAC) explanations. Our algorithm is fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the explanation size limit, maximum feature cardinality, and desired accuracy. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets confirm the theoretical guarantees and show that the spectral explainer outperforms a greedy baseline as the explanation size increases.
articles.title_zh: 学习全球概率解释

articles.title: CoHABIT: Complementary Evaluation of Furniture Layouts through Spatial Rules and Household Routines
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce CoHABIT, a framework for evaluating furniture layouts through complementary spatial rules and household routines. Static assessment captures geometric validity, ergonomic access, functional organization, and configurable design preferences, including Feng Shui. Dynamic assessment uses learned resident policies to simulate everyday activities, resource sharing, coordination, and individual burdens in multi-agent households. Controlled comparisons show how spatial criteria and household behavior reveal distinct aspects of layout quality, while resident profiles and scheduling influence furnishing rankings. Independent verification of household needs grounds dynamic comparisons in observed outcomes, enabling interpretable assessments of how furnished environments serve different households.
articles.title_zh: CoHABIT:通过空间规则和家庭路线对家具布局进行补充评价

articles.title: GeoFusion: An Uncertain Machine Learning Framework for Sensor Fusion
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High positioning precision is a critical requirement in many Global Positioning System (GPS) applications, yet achieving it with affordable smartphone sensors remains an open challenge. Existing approaches treat each GPS observation as an absolute point, discarding the uncertainty inherent in the measurement conditions and leaving the cooperative potential of multiple phones observing the same location untapped. In this work, we propose GeoFusion, a three-stage uncertain machine learning framework for cooperative sensor fusion. In the first stage, each GPS observation is modeled as an uncertain object using one of two proposed models: the volcano function, grounded in satellite geometry, and the empirically derived mountain function, built from the statistical structure of real smartphone data. In the second stage, uncertain objects are clustered by location event using partitional and graph-based algorithms. In the third stage, the cluster output is refined using filter-based and learning-based estimators. Experiments on the Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge dataset show that uncertainty modeling is a primary driver of precision gains: the mountain function significantly outperforms the geometry-only volcano function, and uncertainty-aware UK-medoids significantly outperforms its certain counterpart, k-medoids. A post-clustering deep neural network further refines the cluster estimates, and the recommended configuration achieves a mean absolute error of 2.90 +/- 0.15 meters on held-out test drives, comparable to and on average below the best reported single-phone precision of approximately 3 meters, demonstrating the potential of cooperative uncertainty-aware fusion for affordable GPS sensors.
articles.title_zh: GeoFusion:传感器Fusion的不确定机器学习框架

articles.title: Learning Acceptable Lotteries via Queries: Minimizing Aggregated Violation Distances
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When deploying an AI system, a developer can randomize over several candidate versions, sending each request to a version chosen at random, to balance the requirements of multiple stakeholders. We study a setting in which each of $n$ stakeholders reveals only whether a proposed lottery over $m$ candidates is acceptable, and each stakeholder's acceptable lotteries lie on one side of an unknown hyperplane. While previous work sought a lottery that every stakeholder accepts, such a lottery need not exist when, for instance, safety and helpfulness requirements are in conflict. We therefore minimize a power mean of the stakeholders' violations; since binary answers reveal neither the size of a violation nor how to compare violations across stakeholders, we measure each violation by a normalized distance to the stakeholder's acceptance boundary. We characterize exactly when accept/reject answers determine these distances. When they do, $\mathcal{O}(nm\log(1/\varepsilon))$ queries suffice to learn them, where $\varepsilon$ is the precision of the utilities, and this bound is tight; when they do not, a natural worst-case approach is optimal up to a constant factor, even compared with methods that make unlimited queries. For limited query budgets, we give a sampling algorithm whose number of queries for a given accuracy does not depend on $n$, and show that a deterministic algorithm cannot guarantee a small loss without querying almost all stakeholders. Synthetic experiments illustrate the resulting tradeoff between querying many stakeholders and learning each of them accurately.
articles.title_zh: 通过查询学习可接受彩票:尽量减少累计违规距离

articles.title: From Learning Rates to Rotational Schedules: Finite-Horizon Theory on the Sphere
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How should step sizes be scheduled across a finite training horizon? Cosine and warmup-stable-decay (WSD) schedules are widely adopted in large-scale pretraining, yet their effect on optimization also depends on parameter norms. Normalization can make parameter groups scale invariant, so that the loss depends only on their direction, while their norms still affect how fast the parameters rotate. In this work, we formulate schedule design directly in the space of rotational motion. Working within a geodesically convex spherical setting, we derive a last-iterate convergence guarantee for arbitrary rotational schedules that separates their overall scale from their distribution over time. We derive the unique schedule that minimizes this bound and prove that it approaches linear decay as the horizon grows. Empirically, our rotational interpretation and idealized spherical analysis provide useful predictions for LLM pretraining in practice, including schedule comparisons missed by existing analyses. Our analysis predicts schedule ordering across model scales for both vanilla (Adam, Muon) and Hyperball-style (AdamH, MuonH) optimizers. Our Hyperball experiments support the predicted strong performance of linear LR decay and confirm our prediction that WSD underperforms in this setting. Accounting for parameter norm dynamics, we predict instead the strong performance of WSD for Adam and Muon shown in practice. Guided by our theoretical insights, we also derive a new LR schedule for Adam and Muon, which improves over the established cosine and WSD schedules. All in all, these results support the use of rotational dynamics to understand, predict, and ultimately guide scheduling in LLM pretraining.
articles.title_zh: 从学习率到自旋时间表:有限范围 球体理论

articles.title: How Multi-Timescale Memory Cools Optimization: Theory and Evidence from AdEMAMix
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Augmenting AdamW with multiple momentum timescales improves large language model pretraining, yet the mechanism driving these gains remains poorly understood. We identify an interaction between multi-timescale optimizer memory and the geometry of normalized networks: memory changes parameter norms and thereby controls how fast parameters rotate. Starting from exact norm dynamics under decoupled weight decay, we show that the parameter norm depends on the temporal correlation of the updates, with weight decay controlling how long these correlations influence optimization. We show how an independently weighted slow momentum can substantially increase the norm of parameters, while contributing negligible power to the instantaneous update, therefore acting as an endogenous annealing schedule. We study this mechanism in AdEMAMix for language-model pretraining. Controlled interventions show that this scheduling mechanism has clear practical consequences and is an important factor behind AdEMAMix's advantage over AdamW.
articles.title_zh: 多时尺度记忆如何冷却优化:理论与证据来自AdEMAMix

articles.title: Aggregation Dispersion: An Information-Geometric Diagnostic of Oversmoothing in Graph Neural Networks
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Message-passing neural networks (MPNNs) learn node representations by iteratively aggregating information from neighbors, but stacking too many layers causes all representations to converge, an effect known as oversmoothing. We propose a geometric perspective on this phenomenon. At each depth $k$, the propagation operator assigns to every node $v$ a walk distribution $p_v^{(k)}$, a probability distribution over source nodes. These walk distributions form a point cloud on the probability simplex, whose contraction to a single point characterizes complete mixing of the propagation operator, and thus oversmoothing. To measure this contraction, we use the Fisher-Rao metric, the unique Riemannian metric on the simplex invariant up to scale under sufficient statistics, whose scaled chordal distance under the square-root embedding $p \mapsto \sqrt{p}$ is the Hellinger distance. The resulting diagnostic, the aggregation dispersion $D_k$, is the variance of the embedded point cloud on the unit sphere. We prove that: (i) $D_k = 0$ if and only if the $k$-th step propagation matrix has rank one, a necessary and sufficient condition for complete operator mixing; (ii) $D_k$ is non-increasing with depth; (iii) the spectral gap of the propagation matrix controls the rate of this decay; and (iv) for contractive MPNNs, the aggregation dispersion upper-bounds the representation dispersion up to graph- and initialization-dependent constants. Across 14 model configurations and 11 datasets, $D_k$ attains the highest mean absolute Pearson correlation with test accuracy across depths among eight diagnostics ($|r| = 0.721$, using log-transformed diagnostic values), numerically comparable to the post-training effective rank ($|r| = 0.688$), while requiring no training.
articles.title_zh: 综合散射:图神经网络中过度流出的信息地理诊断

articles.title: Attacking Tabular Foundation Models: An Experimental Taxonomy of Context Poisoning and Test-Time Evasion
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tabular foundation models condition predictions on labeled examples supplied at inference time, creating an attack surface that differs from conventional model training. We study four manipulation families (label flipping, backdoor context poisoning, clean-label context selection, and test-time evasion) and organize them by attack stage, label consistency, and distributional realism. TabPFN-2.5, TabICL, and XGBoost are evaluated on CIC-IDS2017 and N-BaIoT using a common preprocessing and evaluation pipeline. Backdoor context poisoning provides strong targeted control over the in-context models with little change in clean accuracy, whereas selecting real, correctly labeled boundary-crowding rows causes no systematic accuracy degradation up to a 20% bias fraction. A simplified surrogate-transfer constrained PGD attack inspired by, but not equivalent to, CAPGD also produces test-time evasion, outperforming equal-budget random noise in most settings. The comparison shows that attack effectiveness depends strongly on both where manipulation occurs and how much freedom the attacker has to alter the data.
articles.title_zh: 攻击台表基础模型:毒性和试验-时间泄漏的实验分类

articles.title: How Seasonal Reference Choice Changes the Apparent Gains of Chronos Models in Electricity Load Forecasting
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a forecasting model is said to beat a simple baseline, the size of that win depends on which baseline was used. We measure how much this matters for two zero-shot foundation models, Chronos-Bolt and Chronos-2, on hourly electricity load. The study uses 60 fixed cases drawn from eight series in four public collections, with forecasts 24 and 168 hours ahead and up to 2,048 hours of history. Each model is compared with daily persistence, weekly persistence, a weekday hybrid, a daily-weekly blend, and a reference chosen from these on a validation period. We keep every origin-level forecast and estimate uncertainty with paired circular block bootstrap intervals using 168- and 336-hour blocks. A week ahead, Bolt clearly beats weekly persistence in 21 of 30 cases but the validation-selected reference in only 14, and its median gain falls from 17.3% to 11.9%. For Chronos-2 the clear-win counts are 18 and 15. Chronos-2 has lower week-ahead MAE than Bolt in 24 cases, yet only 12 of those differences are clear. The selected reference is not always the harder baseline, since on some test windows it does worse than weekly persistence. The choice of baseline therefore changes both how large the reported gain is and how sure we can be of it. The results are exploratory: the series and windows are related, an earlier pilot was inspected, pretraining overlap cannot be ruled out, and the case-level intervals are not corrected for multiple comparisons.
articles.title_zh: 季节参考选择如何改变Chronos模型在电力负荷预测中的明显收益

articles.title: Exact on Paper: Which LLM Serving Shortcuts Flip Graded Answers, Measured Against the Noise of Reordering the Same Requests
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Teams enable serving features such as prefix caching, chunked prefill and speculative decoding after checking that benchmark accuracy is unchanged, because the engine documents them as exact. Accuracy is an aggregate, so a feature can hold it while flipping which requests are answered correctly. We serve one 4B instruction model in vLLM under nine single feature configurations and five replicas of a reference configuration, grade 3,380 requests from five benchmarks in every run, and compare each candidate with a restart floor (fresh process) and a scheduling floor (same requests in a different order). With default kernels every configuration keeps accuracy within one point, and the seven exact features flip the graded outcome of 1.47% (95% CI 1.13 to 1.85) to 1.78% (1.39 to 2.20) of requests, none above the scheduling floor of 1.72%, while the FP8 KV cache flips 3.36% (2.80 to 3.96), as many as FP8 weights. With batch invariant kernels all seven exact features, speculative decoding included, reproduce the reference text on every request, while the FP8 KV cache still flips 3.91% (3.28 to 4.53) of graded outcomes. A gate that compares against a single replica pair rejected an unchanged configuration, so we recommend certifying a serving change under batch invariant kernels, where the floor is zero, or against a scheduling floor measured from at least three replicas.
articles.title_zh: 纸张上的精确度: 哪个 LLM 提供快捷键 翻转分级的答案, 根据重排相同请求的噪音测量

articles.title: CrysLDM: Latent Diffusion Model for Crystal Material Generation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating new crystal materials with desirable chemical properties has long been a challenging task. Existing diffusion models operate in feature space, requiring complex diffusion architectures to model the joint distribution of atom types, coordinates, and lattice structures. This complexity increases the number of diffusion steps, leading to higher training and sampling costs. In this work, we aim to generate novel crystal materials within a time- and resource-constrained setup, where existing models are not well-suited. To address this, we propose CrysLDM, a novel latent diffusion model for 3D crystal materials, which integrates a variational autoencoder and a diffusion model. The VAE encoder maps 3D crystal structures into a latent space, where the diffusion model operates. Since CrysLDM leverages a smooth, lower-dimensional latent space, it simplifies the generative process and accelerates both training and inference. Through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets and tasks, we show that CrysLDM generates stable and valid materials with quality comparable to state-of-the-art methods, while being significantly more efficient in terms of computational resources and time.
articles.title_zh: CrysLDM:晶体材料生成的晚期扩散模型

articles.title: Towards Global Counterfactual-Based Self-Explainable Graph Neural Networks
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph Counterfactual Explanations (GCEs) have emerged as an effective approach for interpreting Graph Neural Network (GNN) predictions by identifying minimal graph modifications needed to change predictions. However, existing methods suffer from two fundamental limitations: (1) They rely on a post-hoc explanation paradigm, where a separate explainer is trained after the GNN. This sequential optimization prevents the explainer from leveraging how the GNN learned its representations, often resulting in lower-quality explanations. (2) They are largely local, generating counterfactual explanations only for individual samples. Consequently, they fail to capture generalizable patterns across the data distribution, a crucial gap for applications like drug discovery, where global principles enable systematic decision-making across thousands of cases. To address these limitations, we propose GCSGNN (Global Counterfactual-based Self-explainable GNN), a unified framework that integrates counterfactual generation into the GNN architecture, encouraging explanations that faithfully reflect the model's decision-making process. Beyond local explanations, GCSGNN discovers shared latent patterns influencing predictions across graphs, yielding global (i.e., model-level) counterfactual explanations. We further introduce an efficient latent-space counterfactual mechanism that avoids the combinatorial complexity of discrete graph manipulation, enabling scalable discovery of generalizable modification patterns. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that GCSGNN outperforms existing methods in generating effective counterfactual explanations. Our code is available at https://github.com/wendyzheng22/gcsgnn.
articles.title_zh: 走向全球反事实自解图神经网络

articles.title: Learning-Augmented QUBO for Time-Expanded Multi-Commodity Flow
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study energy-aware multi-commodity flow on time-expanded graphs, a problem that captures dynamic routing in layered networks and is NP-hard in general. We formulate the problem as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization problem, give an explicit penalty coefficient that provably guarantees feasibility, and show that it is smaller than the standard bound by a factor of roughly the number of active links. The layered structure of the time-expanded graph yields three structural results: a treewidth bound that gives a fixed-parameter tractable exact algorithm in the bag size, a matrix-product-operator representation of small bond dimension, and a proof that the annealing gap of the associated Ising Hamiltonian is strictly positive for every instance with a unique optimum, uniformly over bounded windows. For learning-augmented routing, we bound the Hamming distance between a predicted and an optimal flow by the flow error, and prove a consistency guarantee: a hybrid algorithm that keeps the better of the prediction and the solver output returns a flow whose cost exceeds the optimum by a factor that grows linearly with the prediction error. The results are exact statements about the QUBO and its associated Ising Hamiltonian, and they hold for any physical implementation.
articles.title_zh: 时间扩展多商品流动的学习强化QUBO

articles.title: LAF-ECG: Multi-Resolution Lead-Aware Fusion of Time-Series and Language Foundation Models for ECG Classification
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation has advanced substantially with deep learning, yet many methods remain task-specific and label-dependent. Large language models (LLMs) and time-series foundation models (TSFMs) offer complementary pretrained representations, but integrating them is challenging because of mismatched feature spaces and the lead- and scale-dependent structure of ECG signals. We propose LAF-ECG (Lead-Aware Foundation Fusion for ECG), a dual-foundation framework that extends MedTsLLM with a lead-aware interface to a frozen TSFM backbone while retaining its reprogramming pathway. The proposed framework captures multi-resolution temporal context, fuses temporal and language-aligned ECG representations through adaptive residual integration, and employs branch-specific supervision with cross-branch alignment. LAF-ECG achieves 71.10% accuracy and 62.43% macro-F1 on PTB-XL, and 89.73% accuracy and 65.94% macro-F1 on Chapman-Shaoxing, outperforming MedTsLLM on both datasets. These results highlight the value of preserving lead-specific temporal structure when combining temporal and language foundation representations for ECG classification. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/kkianamm/LAF-ECG.
articles.title_zh: LAF-ECG:多分辨率铅 -- -- 对时间序列和语言基础进行整合的ECG分类模型

articles.title: Deterministic Proper Positive-Only Learning Is Independent of ZFC
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Binary classification from positive-only samples is a variant of PAC learning in which the learner receives i.i.d. samples only from the positive region of an unknown target concept, but is evaluated on the full distribution. Improper learnability in this model has a textbook characterization, whereas proper learnability has remained open for decades. Recent work characterized it for learners with access to randomness, and showed that, unlike in PAC learning, some classes are properly learnable with randomness but not without it, leaving the deterministic case open. We show that this case cannot be resolved within the standard axioms of mathematics (ZFC): there is a class of VC dimension two whose deterministic proper learnability is independent of ZFC, even though a randomized learner provably learns it. Moreover, no dimension of finite character, a desirable property shared by most dimensions in learning theory, characterizes deterministic proper learnability. We also show that the size of the domain is decisive. In ZFC, deterministic proper learnability has a combinatorial characterization on every domain whose cardinality is below a certain threshold, including every countable domain. In contrast, this characterization fails on every domain of sufficiently large cardinality. Under the generalized continuum hypothesis, this threshold is sharp: it is the exact cardinality at which the characterization starts to fail. Finally, our proofs introduce new tools, based on the Erdos--Rado partition theorem, that may be of broader interest.
articles.title_zh: 决定性 正确的正面 - 唯一学习是独立于 ZFC

articles.title: What Should World Models Plan Over? Learning Geometry-Aligned Representations of Body Motion
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce MotionPort, which learns low-dimensional latent representations of body motion for accurate dynamics prediction and effective long-horizon planning. Existing world-model planners often search over action representations learned for prediction, yet we show that predictive accuracy alone does not ensure that optimization can discover successful trajectories. MotionPort addresses this mismatch by representing body trajectories rather than action chunks and organizing the search space by motion similarity, helping predicted improvements translate into successful execution. Without fine-tuning state encoders, MotionPort raises average goal-reaching success from 37.9% to 87.8% across three backbones and seven settings in four domains. On the evaluated AntMaze-OGBench tasks, it achieves 72% success, compared with 4% for the strongest baseline.
articles.title_zh: 世界模式计划应该结束吗? 学习几何-身体运动的相通表现

articles.title: probly: Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As machine learning systems are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, the question of how to represent and quantify uncertainty has moved from a methodological side issue to a central concern. In practice, however, making a model uncertainty-aware is still surprisingly difficult: relevant tools tend to be scattered across libraries, each tied to a particular framework and a particular approach to modeling uncertainty, and the choice of representation, quantification, and evaluation is typically left to the user without much guidance. In this paper, we present probly, a Python package that addresses these issues in a single, modular framework. probly offers (i) lightweight transformations that turn existing models into uncertainty-aware ones, currently supporting PyTorch, scikit-learn, and Flax, (ii) several representations, including second-order distributions, credal sets, and conformal prediction, (iii) the corresponding quantification measures, and (iv) a number of evaluation protocols, which can be combined more or less arbitrarily. Using probly, we conduct a benchmark study on three standard tasks --- selective prediction, out-of-distribution detection, and active learning. In addition, and unlike existing benchmarks, we evaluate suitable methods on first-order data, i.e., datasets for which the target itself is a distribution over outcomes. We further illustrate the flexibility of the package on a number of less standard case studies, including large language models, graph neural networks, and data streams. The package is publicly available at https://github.com/pwhofman/probly.
articles.title_zh: 概率: 不确定- 智能机器学习

articles.title: Selecting Stable Sampling Dynamics for Compositional Diffusion: A Feynman-Kac Weight Reduction
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given $K$ separately trained diffusion models, how should one sample from a $\beta_k$-weighted product of their terminal laws without jointly retraining the experts? Existing Feynman--Kac constructions provide many weighted stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with the correct target marginal. The consequential question is how to select useful proposal dynamics among them. We study an explicit family of weighted diffusions that realizes the same product-of-intermediate-experts trajectory. A scalar parameter $\lambda$ controls how strongly the proposal drift follows the composed expert score, while an additional Langevin component can be varied independently. Writing $B=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\beta_k>0$, we identify the distinguished choice $\lambda=1/B$. At this value, the aggregate squared-score term in the instantaneous Feynman--Kac log-weight rate cancels exactly. For positive expert exponents, the remaining score-disagreement contribution is non-positive. We call this structural cancellation Feynman--Kac reduction. Under bounded-divergence assumptions, it yields an upper bound on the instantaneous unnormalized log-weight rate for all $\lambda\leq 1/B$. For linear diffusion protocols with compactly supported expert data, $\lambda=1/B$ yields two-sided bounds at every nonterminal time, for exponents of either sign. A corresponding result holds for a single expert under the same divergence assumption. In these two-sided settings, the selected value is unique within the specified family in a universal worst-case sense. Experiments on Gaussian mixtures and molecular sampling compare the analytically predicted stability with actual sampling quality, including instances in which parameter choices different from $\lambda=1/B$ perform better empirically.
articles.title_zh: 选择结构分散的稳定取样动态:一个Feynman-Kac减重

articles.title: Constrained Diffusion from Binary Evaluations via Learned Doob h-Functions
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conditional generation under constraints that can only be checked on a finished sample, such as a molecular property filter, remains challenging for diffusion models: most guidance methods require differentiable measurement operators, paired conditional data, or rollouts of the base model at every step. We present a framework grounded in the Doob $h$-transform that reduces conditional generation to learning a single function, the probability that a noisy sample denoises into the constraint set. We learn this function from binary clean-sample evaluations alone, by squared-error regression on forward-noised labels; the base model is frozen, one lightweight head is trained per constraint, and noisy-state classifier guidance arises as a special case. The exact guidance step fades where the constraint signal provably vanishes and carries a factor of the inverse probability across samples, which normalized guidance discards: with the schedule and mean step size held fixed, equalizing the step costs 17.0 to 18.5 points of constraint satisfaction on CIFAR-10 at comparable FID, across independently trained estimators. Guidance is more than 50$\times$ cheaper per satisfying sample than rejection sampling at a 1.7% base rate, raises a Lipinski-type property filter on QM9 from 54.3% to 96.8%, and lifts satisfaction on Stable Diffusion 1.5 from 7.2% to 60.0% at one sixteenth of the cost of derivative-free selection, which reaches 9.0%. These results demonstrate that binary evaluations of clean samples are sufficient supervision for constrained generation across pixel, latent, and molecular diffusion.
articles.title_zh: 通过学习多布h-功能限制二进制评价的传播

articles.title: Learning Gaussian Process Priors with Linear Semigroups and Kinetic Regularisation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a semigroup-based construction of Gaussian process (GP) priors. A linear semigroup transforms a source GP at $t=0$ into a prior at $t=1$, enabling computationally tractable regression. Linearity preserves Gaussianity, allowing us to characterise the evolution of the covariance and draw connections with optimal transport and convolution models.
