On 21 vision-text encoder pairs and five seeds, pooled fitting aligns every pair, whereas pairwise fits fail in 68 of 105 pair-seed cells. Mean alignment error (FOSCTTM) falls from 0.1457 to 0.0099, and zero-shot accuracy nearly doubles on ten datasets. Gains persist across the tested within-modality pooling constructions with a WP bridge. New corpora reuse the bridge through native maps fitted to unlabeled target features from every source encoder. Agreement with separately fitted reference maps detects failures on COCO.
articles.title_zh: 从对等到集体:编码器收藏 使未发光-语言对齐可靠

articles.title: PSC-Gen: Physical Sequence Conditioning for Video Generation via Agentic Visual Planning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in video diffusion models have enabled the synthesis of high-fidelity, visually compelling videos. However, despite being trained on internet-scale video data, understanding underlying physical laws and generating physically plausible dynamics remain challenging. To mitigate this, conditioning video generators on explicit physical reasoning has emerged as a promising direction. Nevertheless, existing conditioning approaches often fail to incorporate detailed physical guidance into generation, resulting in physically implausible motion or visual artifacts. We propose PSC-Gen, a training-free framework that employs an agentic approach to synthesize visual conditions and inject their core dynamics via low-frequency filtering. By iteratively planning physical states and verifying generated keyframes, our Physics Agent constructs visually and physically consistent keyframe sequences. We then interpolate these keyframes into a continuous physical sequence and inject only its low-frequency components, steering the video model to preserve physical dynamics while synthesizing fine visual details. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations across physics-informed and robotic manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that PSC-Gen faithfully follows instructions and generates physically plausible videos.
articles.title_zh: PSC-Gen:通过代理视觉规划为视频生成设定物理序列条件

articles.title: Frozen by the Mean: Early Temporal Guidance Unfreezes Motion in Video Diffusion Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video diffusion models can render convincing frames while failing to produce the requested action. Increasing classifier-free guidance (CFG) can strengthen motion, but also saturates and shifts colors. Scalar CFG assigns the same coefficient to the averaged and frame-varying components of its prediction difference, limiting independent control of temporal variation. THAW, Temporal Harmonic Amplification during Warm-up, retains stock CFG and adds a separately weighted residual during an initial denoising window. Its dose specifies the added norm relative to the current CFG difference, giving the extra guidance a consistent relative budget across sampling steps. THAW is training-free and reuses CFG's two model predictions with an unchanged network evaluation count. It improves cost-matched motion over scalar and scheduled CFG on five video models, with positive point estimates against existing guidance methods on three of them. On VBench, THAW raises dynamic degree by about 14 to 15 points over stock CFG while increasing total scores on a different set of three models.
articles.title_zh: 由平分冻结: 早期时间指导 解冻视频传播模型中的动作

articles.title: Contrastive Gradient Guidance for Test-Time Multi-Preference Alignment of Diffusion Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aligning pre-trained diffusion models with multiple context-dependent preferences requires adapting generation at test time rather than relying on offline fine-tuning, which requires hyperparameter tuning and a new training run for each preference trade-off. Existing approaches compress diverse preferences into a single scalar reward objective for fine-tuning or test-time guidance rather than directly reusing existing generative experts released for different purposes and obtained through different fine-tuning methods. In this work, we propose Contrastive Gradient Guidance (CGG), a test-time compositional generative framework that reformulates multi-preference alignment as a composition of distributions. CGG represents each preference as a contrastive preference pair of favored experts and unfavored anti-experts, whose score difference forms a contrastive gradient guidance signal that combines denoising directions (gradients) from off-the-shelf diffusion models during sampling. Experiments show that CGG reuses pre-trained and fine-tuned models as favored experts or anti-experts to control output style and safety, and that it can be combined with existing sampling-based reward guidance. With a single fixed scale per pair, CGG composes five preferences at once and gives a more balanced trade-off across text-image preference, concept control, photographic fidelity, and safety than offline fine-tuning, weight-space merging, and reward steering.
articles.title_zh: 测试-时间多优先对接传播模式的对比性渐进性指导

articles.title: JevNavAgent: A Single-Forward Visual Navigation Agent with Trajectory-Level RL for Gigapixel Pathology
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs) exceed single-pass vision-language model (VLM) capacity at cellular resolution, while multiple instance learning relies on query-agnostic offline patching without interactive reasoning. Multi-step VLM navigation agents inspect regions on demand, yet face two bottlenecks: (1) autoregressive action decoding incurs heavy latency, throttling exploration and online multi-trajectory RL; and (2) offline distillation suffers from an existential-versus-universal stopping asymmetry between positive detection and negative exclusion, inducing thumbnail and kinematic shortcuts while leaving policies prone to passing metastases without stopping. Under the Jev (System One) paradigm, a model predicts distributions over predefined decision spaces in one forward pass (0 generated tokens) while deterministic code executes navigation. We build JevNavAgent, a 2B-parameter agent combining factorized stopping, spatial-candidate, and contextual-bilinear answer heads with overview modality dropout. We pair Stage-1 offline counterfactual trajectory alignment (mitigating depth and panning shortcuts) with Stage-2 online trajectory-level GRPO (Traj-GRPO), using decoding-free rollouts to optimize branch-level lesion discovery, in-polygon stopping, and step-wise confidence gain. On Clean Visual WSI-VQA, JevNavAgent achieves 51.57% multi-scale (50.43% terminal-step) overall and 51.39% focal accuracy, outperforming frontier VLM agents and 4B-11B open-source cascades while running nearly 12x faster than frontier APIs (5.63s vs. 66.64-70.04s). On CAMELYON16 Official Test, Traj-GRPO reaches 22.45% localization (converting 11/12, or 91.7%, of visited tumors into grounded stops) with 93.75% specificity and 69.77% slide accuracy, surpassing Stage-1 SFT under matched stopping rules alongside zero-shot budget scaling.
articles.title_zh: JevNav Agent:一个具有轨道-水平RL的单向视觉导航代理,用于Gigapixel病理学

articles.title: AdapToC: A Unified Framework for Multi-Task Visual Token Communication
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pretrained discrete visual tokenizers supply compact latents for synthesis, recognition, and embodied perception, yet wireless token streaming remains fragile. Under fading and noisy pilots, hard cyclic redundancy check (CRC) erasures turn corrupted blocks into missing tokens while frozen decoders amplify edge errors, which can collapse unequal error protection (UEP) into a binary choice between strong coding and omission under severe fading. Soft bit posteriors break this collapse. We present AdapToC, a single-pass transceiver that restores multi-tier rate-distortion tradeoffs without altering tokenizer weights or differentiating through pixel decoders. We align codebook geometry to the channel via offline frequency-weighted Pseudo-Gray relabeling and Halton dispersion to contract bit and burst errors with zero overhead. Because soft recovery pulls intermediate rates onto the three-tier convex hull, our unit-gated AdaLN sender schedules protection tiers across channel budgets, while our pilot-calibrated receiver feeds factorized codebook posteriors into a ConvNeXt-attention restorer with CRC bypass. We co-train AdapToC solely in latent space via counterfactual utility estimation and codebook cross-entropy regularization. On identical VQGAN-f16 tokens, AdapToC outperforms TONIC and adaptive TokenCom+AMC, cuts multi-SNR Rayleigh LPIPS from 0.6551 to 0.3312 within the frozen-tokenizer PSNR ceiling, and saves 43.8% Rician-K6 symbols at matched quality. Our single-pass restorer runs 8.3x faster than iterative resampling, raises accuracy while accelerating decoder-free recognition 20.6x, and improves fidelity plug-and-play across TiTok, VAR, and zero-shot NuPlan.
articles.title_zh: AdapTOC: 多任务视觉托肯通信的统一框架

articles.title: Where Does a Weight-Editing Agent Help? Blind Diagnosis and Repair of Deployment Faults in Vision Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language-model agents can read and edit the weights of neural networks without gradients, and this is increasingly presented as a new way of repairing models. We ask what such an agent adds, in a setting with a known answer. A vision model moved into a new system may be broken by a preprocessing, weight-conversion or output-convention fault; an agent restricted to forward passes must decide whether a fault exists, name it, and undo it by editing the weights. Over 183 runs on classification, segmentation and detection, scored against the fault-free model, we find three things. When the kind of fault is known, the agent is not needed: a script written afterwards repairs 30 of 48 faults against the agent's 33. But the agent did not have to be told: on five fault types outside every script it repairs 15 of 15 where that script repairs 4, and it never edits any of 21 fault-free models. And its limits are predictable: it needs a trustworthy per-layer reference for the model's activations and a fault that is an invertible structured transformation; without them, small faults are missed and repairs stay partial. We derive guidance on when to use an agent and when a script.
articles.title_zh: 哪里有重量编辑员帮助? 视力模型中的盲诊断和部署缺陷修复

articles.title: 3DCodeFactory: Scaling Training Data for 3D Code Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As code agents evolve, their scope is expanding from generating simple static 3D meshes to constructing structurally complete, complex, interactive 3D scenes. However, existing datasets mainly rely on converting or captioning pre-existing 3D assets, consisting mostly of single-turn code data for static single objects and struggling to scale task diversity and scene complexity, leaving such training data scarce. We present 3DCodeFactory, an automated framework that directly constructs diverse, complex 3D training data from abundant raw text (e.g., diffusion prompts and product descriptions). The framework first leverages an image generator to synthesize 3D reference images from raw text as visual anchors, guiding the generation of concrete modeling specifications and interactive functional requirements; meanwhile, it jointly constructs visual, specification, and functional rubrics from the reference images and requirements to automatically score and filter multi-turn agent rollouts. Based on this framework, we release 3DCodeFactory-Data, comprising 5,045 high-quality task instances and multi-turn interaction trajectories. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.8-27B on 3DCodeFactory-Data significantly improves performance on BlenderWorld, P3D-Bench, and 3DCodeBench, consistently outperforming models trained on existing open-source 3D code datasets, with our 27B model further surpassing the same-series 2.4T flagship Qwen3.8-Max in overall performance.
articles.title_zh: 3DCodeFactory: 三维代码代理的扩展培训数据

articles.title: ArgsWorld: Unifying 3DGS Scene Reconstruction, Generation and Extrapolation with Autoregressive Diffusion Transformer
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autoregressive diffusion world models deliver strong video generation performance, yet they typically output only RGB frames rather than explicit 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) scene representations, creating a gap between learned visual world dynamics and usable 3D assets for downstream robotics, simulation and rendering. To bridge this gap, we introduce ArgsWorld, an autoregressive diffusion model that also produces an explicit 3DGS scene. For each generation chunk, the diffusion transformer jointly processes clean historical image latents and noisy latents for new views. It keeps the historical image latents fixed and refreshes the scene features so that the Gaussian representation can be revised as new regions come into view. Our 3D Self-Forcing Distillation trains the model on its own generated histories using a mixture of single-view and multi-view data. Distribution matching supervises direct image latents and latents of Gaussian renderings at both generation and additional cameras. ArgsWorld unifies 3D scene reconstruction from posed images, scene generation from image or text prompts, and scene extrapolation across camera segments with disconnected endpoints. Experimental results demonstrate that ArgsWorld achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple 3D scene modeling tasks. Project page: https://m4a1tastegood.github.io/ArgsWorld/
articles.title_zh: argsWorld: 将 3DGS 场景重建、生成和外推与自动扩散变形器统一

articles.title: Inference Dynamics: Image Classifiers Keep Using Visual Cues After They Are Removed
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Image classifiers are typically evaluated by their final predictions, treating inference as a static image-to-label mapping. Reliability, however, also depends on whether a model can relinquish evidence after that evidence disappears. We reveal a counterintuitive phenomenon: removing a local visual cue from its original location may not remove its influence on the prediction. Once captured by early layers, the cue can become distributed across later representations, making ``no longer visible'' different from ``no longer relied upon.'' We introduce Inference Dynamics, a process-level framework for tracing how cue influence evolves and remains withdrawable across network depth. Given an image and a matched cue-removed reference, we replace cue-aligned states in the original branch with their reference counterparts at successive layers and measure recovery toward the cue-free prediction. The resulting trajectory separates evidence locality from decision-level withdrawability. Across datasets and architectures, we find locality declines before withdrawability collapses: cue-induced information becomes less concentrated at its original support while its effect remains active, before entering an evidence lock-in stage. Consequently, fixed late-stage correction may alter the final readout without removing accumulated cue dependence. We therefore propose Evidence Reset, which selects an input-dependent layer before lock-in and reconstructs cue-aligned states toward their cue-free counterparts. Our results establish evidence withdrawability as a process-level dimension of classifier reliability and suggest a new intervention principle: correction depth should follow the dynamics of evidence rather than be fixed in advance.

articles.title: NavDecision: Parallel Multi-Step Action Prediction with Persistent Self-Referential Learning for Vision-and-Language Navigation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires timely decisions based on instructions and visual observations. However, autoregressive VLN models generate action descriptions token by token, introducing substantial inference overhead. Decision models offer an efficient alternative but face challenges in maintaining short-horizon action coherence and long-horizon goal alignment. To address these challenges, we propose NavDecision, an efficient multi-step VLN decision model. We introduce parallel multi-step action prediction (PMAP) to predict multiple action distributions from a shared vision-language state, and memory-augmented self-referential policy optimization (M-SRPO) to learn from unsuccessful trajectories using successful trajectories as references. A cross-iteration success memory further accumulates historical successful trajectories to provide informative training feedback. NavDecision achieves success rates of 64.60% on R2R-CE and 64.57% on RxR-CE with a 4B backbone. Compared with existing autoregressive VLN methods, it delivers significant inference speedups of up to $22.28\times$ and $18.96\times$ while maintaining comparable navigation performance.
articles.title_zh: 导航决定:平行的多步骤行动预测与远景和语言导航的持续自我参考学习

articles.title: Not All Directions Are Flat: Decomposed-Gradient Flatness for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many applications of novel view synthesis, such as augmented reality and robotics, can afford only a few input views, since dense capture is costly. With such sparse views, however, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) overfits the training views and degrades at unseen viewpoints. Among the approaches to this problem, flat-minima optimization treats the Gaussians as trainable parameters and steers training toward flat minima, which generalize better, by perturbing the Gaussians with random noise or along the training gradient. However, these perturbations ignore their direction relative to the other training views. Interestingly, we find that the direction of the perturbation determines whether it improves generalization. Specifically, we decompose the gradient of each training view into a component parallel to the average gradient of all views, on which the views agree, and an orthogonal component, on which they disagree. Perturbing along the orthogonal component improves generalization, whereas perturbing along the parallel component does not. We further find that the flatness correction often opposes the reconstruction gradient, shrinking or even reversing the reconstruction step. Based on these findings, we propose DecoFlat, which perturbs each Gaussian along the orthogonal component together with random noise. Furthermore, we introduce a conflict-aware correction, which removes the part of the flatness correction that opposes the reconstruction gradient, and a rescheduling of the spherical-harmonics color, which suppresses the overfitting of view-dependent appearance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DecoFlat, as a plug-in optimizer, consistently improves vanilla 3DGS and a wide range of sparse-view 3DGS methods.
articles.title_zh: 并非所有方向都是平平的:为 Sparse-View 3D高斯平板

articles.title: ViTrust: Learning 3D Observation Trust for Deformable Physical World Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning deformable physical world models requires dynamics that generalize beyond observed motion. Accurate reconstruction alone does not ensure accurate future prediction, motivating us to learn how observations should influence physical identification. However, visual reliability alone does not determine how informative an observation is about physical dynamics. We propose ViTrust to learn 3D observation trust, determining how strongly each tracked point influences physical identification. Its key design is a visual-contact trust adapter that combines pointwise spatiotemporal evidence with interaction history on a persistent contact graph to predict time-varying observation weights. A single-stage, shared-forward objective jointly optimizes these weights and physical parameters through weighted geometry and correspondence losses, with constraints to prevent observation-weight collapse. All learning uses only the observed prefix. The fitted physics remains fixed for future prediction under supplied controls. Experiments on real-world sequences demonstrate improved future prediction over the evaluated baselines, alongside qualitative demonstrations of novel-control rollouts and cross-object transfer.
articles.title_zh: ViTrust:可变形物理世界模型学习 三维观测信托基金

articles.title: PointNeXt Adapter Improved Model for BIM Component Defect Association under Construction Images and Design Model Attributes
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Construction site defect analysis increasingly requires linking field evidence to the correct BIM object, because a crack, spalling area, missing sleeve or misaligned support is useful for quality control only when it is connected with component identity, location, responsibility and design intent. This paper proposes a PointNeXt Adapter improved model for BIM component defect association under construction images and design model attributes. The method aligns site image crops, local point cloud patches, BIM component identifiers, geometry attributes, material categories, installation stage, inspection distance, viewpoint quality and source reliability tags into component level inspection windows. PointNeXt learns local geometry and deviation from as built point evidence, while the adapter injects BIM attributes so the same geometric irregularity can be interpreted differently for structural, envelope, MEP and embedded components. The fusion head outputs component link, defect class, defect probability, confidence, dominant evidence and recommended review action. A synthetic multisource BIM inspection dataset is used to evaluate repeated layouts, occlusion, sparse point clouds, registration errors and unseen component arrangements. Results show that attribute aware point learning improves association accuracy, defect recall and confidence calibration compared with image only, point only, simple fusion and adapter free baselines. The framework is positioned as traceable BIM issue review support, requiring manual confirmation and staged field validation before operational deployment.
articles.title_zh: PointNEXt 建筑图像和设计模型属性下的BIM组件缺陷协会改进型号

articles.title: Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead for Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models benefit from strong semantic representations that support object recognition and instruction understanding. However, precise manipulation also depends on resolving object locations and workspace relations, and on selecting actions with an estimate of how the scene will evolve. Existing geometry-aware methods make the current scene more explicit, while predictive methods model future observations or representations. Yet future information is often neither grounded in a control-relevant spatial state nor directly used to guide action generation. We introduce Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead (SG-LL), which uses the grounded present as the reference for predicting an actionable near-future representation. A frozen spatial teacher first distills geometric priors into policy-connected spatial tokens. A current-conditioned bottleneck then learns a compact latent that captures future information relative to the present scene. This latent is predicted from the current policy context and initial Action Expert features, without access to future observations or the spatial teacher. Finally, zero-initialized residual fusion incorporates the predicted latent into the Action Expert to refine action generation. Experiments on LIBERO-Plus, CALVIN, and three real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate improvements over in both simulation and real-robot settings.
articles.title_zh: 以空间为基地的Latent Lookahead 展望-语言-行动模型

articles.title: Learning How a Body Moves: Few-Shot Body Inference for Visual World Models of Animated Characters
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two visually identical animated characters can respond differently to the same action command because their body dynamics differ. For example, a stiff blob and its bouncy twin reach different heights when both receive the jump command. Given only the first frame and the action command, a visual world model has no information to distinguish these twins, because their initial appearances are identical. We therefore propose an in-context world model that encodes clips of a character's other actions into a body representation, using a contrastive loss to separate look-alike characters. We introduce ToonTwins, a benchmark of 144 2D cartoon characters that run, jump, fall, turn and crouch. Its characters form look-alike groups of four that differ only in their dynamics profile, and we also evaluate the model on 32 animated animals from DeformingThings4D. Even with a body code from these clips, the latent pixel world model we tested recovered at most 25 percent of the twins' jump height difference. On new shapes, our model identified the correct twin in 85.9 percent of cases, compared with 76.7 percent for a transformer baseline that reads the same clips without a body summary, and in a controlled ablation the contrastive loss gave more than half of this gain. On the animated animals, it reduced the mean path prediction error by 8.5 percent against a model without body information.
articles.title_zh: 学习身体如何移动:视觉世界动画人物模型的少数热身推论

articles.title: MQCODet: Modality Quality-Guided Collaborative Optimization for UAV-Based RGB-T Tiny Pedestrian Detection
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based RGB-thermal (RGB-T) remote sensing provides complementary visual and thermal information for pedestrian perception under complex aerial observation conditions. However, detecting tiny pedestrians in UAV-based RGB-T imagery remains challenging due to cross-modal spatial heterogeneity, manifested as modality quality imbalance and spatial position misalignment. Existing RGB-T detectors primarily address these challenges at the feature fusion stage, without establishing an effective coupling between feature fusion and object localization, potentially resulting in suboptimal detection performance. To address this limitation, we introduce a Modality Quality-Guided Collaborative Optimization Detector (MQCODet), which extends modality quality from a fusion prior to a localization supervision cue. Specifically, we propose a Dynamic Calibration and Region-Aware Fusion (DCRF) module that progressively refines cross-modal spatial alignment and performs region-aware fusion to generate reliable multi-scale features and a scene-level modality quality prior. We further design an Efficient Contextual Interaction (ECI) encoder to enhance multi-scale feature interaction while preserving fine-grained spatial details. Moreover, we propose a Modality-Aware Adaptive (MAA) loss that incorporates the modality prior and object scale to adaptively balance spatial consistency and geometric similarity for localization supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MQCODet surpasses state-of-the-art methods on two UAV-based RGB-T tiny pedestrian detection benchmarks while achieving real-time inference on the edge platform.
articles.title_zh: MQCODet:基于无人驾驶航空器的 RGB-T 小型踏行器检测的 模式质量导向协作优化

articles.title: CivilCADBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Understanding, Reconstructing, and Designing Civil Engineering Drawing Sets
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Civil infrastructure is designed, built, and maintained through engineering drawing sets, yet preparing and revising them remains labour-intensive and calls for automation. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are promising candidates, but assessing them requires a benchmark grounded in real engineering practice. We introduce CivilCADBench, a benchmark for understanding, reconstructing, and designing civil engineering drawing sets, built from real infrastructure drawings and source CAD files containing over 250,000 CAD entities. Unlike parametric 3D CAD models, these drawings are dense, layered, and multi-sheet; and since prints are lossy projections with no pixel trace of layers, a file can print correctly yet remain wrongly organised. CivilCADBench comprises three task families of increasing difficulty: understanding tasks are evaluated with 2,183 expert-reviewed questions ranging from single sheets to whole sets, while reconstruction and design tasks are agentic, requiring models to rebuild printed pages as editable CAD files, either as single pages or entire drawing sets, and to produce new designs. These tasks are performed across 232 pages, 28 sets, and 19 design tasks, and evaluated by a deterministic scorer that compares model outputs with the designers' source files on geometry, layers, text, and dimensions. We evaluate seven frontier MLLMs on CivilCADBench, and find that they read and redraw printed content accurately but recover the file structure poorly: the best model scores above 90% in understanding and single-page reconstruction, yet only 60% on layer assignment and 48% on design. Grounded in real engineering practice, CivilCADBench exposes both the capabilities and the limitations of frontier models in professional civil engineering, laying a foundation for next-generation models and agentic systems for intelligent civil engineering.
articles.title_zh: CivilCABENCH:为了解、重建和设计土木工程绘图装置的多式联运有限责任公司基准

articles.title: KineState-SWAM: A Surgical World Action Model with Explicit Kinematics and Causal Interaction Dynamics
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing surgical world models often leave implicit how instrument motion drives localized tissue responses and how interaction history informs subsequent actions. We introduce KineState-SWAM, a surgical world-action model coupling action prediction and video generation through a persistent interaction state, separating kinematically determined instrument motion from learned scene evolution. A flow-matching policy predicts joint trajectories conditioned on interaction state, robot configuration, and task instruction. Kinematic Geometry Conditioning converts these trajectories into surface-motion tokens and spatially aligned instrument renderings using calibrated URDF kinematics. Causal Interaction Dynamics recurrently updates the state through geometry-guided attention and motion-aligned feature transport, carrying interaction history into subsequent action predictions without intermediate video synthesis. The State-Geometry Adapter combines state-dependent spatial modulation with localized geometric residuals to guide video generation. Interaction-aware supervision emphasizes tissue responses near instrument working regions. We introduce dVRK-Chole5.2k, comprising 5,255 videos spanning 17 surgical tasks. Experiments demonstrate improved action accuracy and video fidelity over evaluated baselines within matched action-conditioning settings. Ablations support preserving and transporting interaction states for long-horizon prediction.
articles.title_zh: Kine State-SWAM:具有明确基内数学和因果关系动态的外科世界行动模型

articles.title: Eidetic Code World Model
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Executable code can preserve a world's structural layout, yet video renderers frequently alter the appearance of previously visited places once they leave the camera view. We present Paintress, a code-conditioned world model that couples an executable geometric proxy with an independently parameterized 3D Gaussian appearance memory in a shared metric coordinate frame. While the proxy enforces structural and visibility constraints, 3D Gaussians capture the visual realization synthesized by emitted observations. To balance stable incremental fusion with consistent readout, Paintress separates writing from reading: newly emitted frames update a persistent raw Gaussian map under confidence-gated selection, whereas a cloned reader copy is globally refined against the observation archive and rendered with coverage masks to condition generation. We also introduce Expedition-33, a benchmark for generated-appearance retention across 11 static scenes, five route families, and 15, 30, and 60 s target absences (165 settings per system). Excluded from the opening image, targets are synthesized during a shared prefix and scored against each system's own first visit at matched return cameras. Across ten systems (1,650 videos), Paintress achieves 0.1220 ROI-LPIPS, 0.0613 MAE, and 52.12% detail retention (vs. 0.2731, 0.1401, and 10.91% for CWM), with lower discrepancy at 60 s (0.1630) than CWM, AgentGarten, and Lyra 2.0 achieve at 15 s.
